title: Minimum Moves to Equal Array Elements
summary: For an integer array nums of size n, determine the least number of moves needed to make all elements equal.
statement: For an integer array nums of size n, determine the least number of moves needed to make all elements equal. In a single move, increase the value of n-1 elements by 1.
constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 100,000; -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; the minimum answer fits a signed 32-bit integer.
One move increments exactly n-1 entries by 1, leaving one entry unchanged.
Return the minimum number of moves to make every entry equal. This is not the single-element increment/decrement variant.
hints: Adding one to all entries does not affect whether they are equal.
Incrementing n-1 entries is equivalent, up to a shared translation, to decrementing the omitted entry.
Reduce every value to the minimum: sum the differences from min(nums).
The answer is sum(nums)-n*min(nums). A one-entry or already-equal array requires zero moves.
editorial: Subtract a common increment after every move: only the omitted entry decreases relative to the rest. With decrements alone, the greatest common target is the initial minimum. Every difference must be removed, yielding the stated formula. The oracle literally explores small normalized n-1-increment states, rather than evaluating the formula.

tests.explanation: Three moves suffice: [1,2,3]→[2,3,3]→[3,4,3]→[4,4,4]. Each move changes two entries.
Incrementing two entries at a time needs 6 moves. A median-based single-element solution would solve a different problem.
